title: Capture the Surrounded Regions

concept.title: Mark what is safe (connected to the border) and capture everything else
body: A board has cells `X` and `O`. A region of `O` cells is *surrounded* if none of its cells touches the border of the board, even through other `O` cells connected by sides. All surrounded regions are captured, that is, turned into `X`. The `O` cells that are connected to a border `O` stay.

This is the enclosed-land task again, with a grid output. Instead of searching from each region and asking whether it reaches the border, **start from the border**: all `O` cells on the border are safe, and a flood fill from them marks all `O` cells that are connected to the border. At the end, every `O` that is not marked is surrounded and becomes `X`.
Notice that the answer is built from the marks: a cell is `O` in the output exactly when it was marked safe (a safe cell is always an `O`), and `X` otherwise. The time is O(h * w).

statement: A board of `h` rows and `w` columns contains the letters `X` and `O`. A group of `O` cells connected through their sides is surrounded if no cell of the group is on the border of the board. Turn all `O` cells of all surrounded groups into `X`, and print the board.
inputFormat: The first line has `h` and `w`: the number of rows and columns.
Each of the next `h` lines has a row of `w` characters.

examples.note: The three O cells in the middle are surrounded and change; the O in the bottom row is on the border and stays.

hints: The O cells on the border, and everything connected to them, are safe.
Flood from all border O cells at once and mark the cells you reach.
In the new board a cell is O only if it was marked.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

h, w = map(int, input().split())
grid = [input().strip() for _ in range(h)]

# Your code here

explanation: A flood fill from all the O cells on the border marks the safe cells; in the output a cell is O exactly when it is marked.
solution.complexity: Time O(h * w), space O(h * w).
